predicate_normalized.semantics: true when the op argument to createBinaryOp is a str; false when op is any other type (typically a callable/lambda). In the ExpressionEvaluator call paths op is always str (derived from type(node.X).__name__); the false branch is only reachable via direct API calls that pass a callable.

public_inputs.name: op
public_inputs.description: The op parameter of CallableParameter.createBinaryOp(cls, lhs, rhs, op). In ALL ExpressionEvaluator paths, op is always a str derived from Python AST node class names via type(node.X).__name__ (e.g., 'Add', 'Gt', 'And', 'min'). The constraint expression strings that feed the AST are hard-coded in TensileBenchmarkCluster.py (lines 283, 288); no CLI flag, YAML key, or env variable supplies the operator name. The non-str branch (callable) is only reachable when createBinaryOp is called directly with a lambda, which occurs only in test code or direct API usage.

derived_symbols.name: op
derived_symbols.derived_from: createBinaryOp parameter. In primary (ExpressionEvaluator) path, op = type(node.op).__name__ (BinOp/BoolOp: Configuration.py:646,653) or type(node.ops[i]).__name__ (Compare: line 661) or self.evaluate(node.func, {}) (Call: line 680). All these produce a str. Constraint strings are hardcoded in TensileBenchmarkCluster.py:283,288 and parsed by ast.parse() in ProjectConfig.addConstraint (Configuration.py:925).

derived_symbols.name: FuncMap
derived_symbols.derived_from: local dict literal inside createBinaryOp; not user-controlled. Its keys are the valid str values of op for the true branch.

derived_symbols.name: expressionStr
derived_symbols.derived_from: argument to ProjectConfig.addConstraint. In production paths: hardcoded string literals in TensileBenchmarkCluster.py ('BenchmarkTaskSize > 0', 'RunDeployStep or RunBenchmarkStep or RunResultsStep'). In the Configuration.py docstring/example (lines 806-810): also hardcoded. No runtime-variable source.

derived_symbols.name: ast_tree
derived_symbols.derived_from: ast.parse(expressionStr, mode='exec') at Configuration.py:925. The tree structure (and hence op type names) is entirely determined by the hardcoded expressionStr.

notes: isinstance is a Python builtin — its behavior is not affected by any external state.
str is the Python builtin str type — also not injectable or configurable.

All four ExpressionEvaluator call sites (lines 647, 654, 662, 681) produce str values for op: the first three use type(node.op).__name__ which always returns a str; line 681 uses self.evaluate(node.func, {}) on a Name node with empty context, which returns str(node.id) — always a str.

The false branch (op is callable) is only reachable by callers that bypass ExpressionEvaluator and invoke createBinaryOp directly with a lambda. This pattern appears in test_Configuration.py:734 and test_configuration_char.py:196.

The constraint expression strings are hardcoded constants in TensileBenchmarkCluster.py and not derived from CLI, YAML, env, filesystem, or GPU probe at runtime. Therefore this predicate has no genuine public inputs that vary across user invocations — its outcome (True) in production is fully determined at development time.
